purpose: Concept mockups for discussion; replace illustrative screens with actual release-build captures before App Store submission.

directions.name: Soft editorial
directions.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: concept contact sheet for Simplist's iOS App Store screenshots. This is a design exploration, not final submission artwork.
Primary request: Create one polished wide image presenting EXACTLY FIVE separate tall portrait App Store screenshot designs side by side in a single horizontal row. Each panel must have a true approximately 9:19.5 portrait proportion, equal size, with narrow clean gutters. Overall image approximately 2.4:1 landscape, high resolution. No perspective on the contact sheet. Show all five complete panels with their full headline and device.
Brand reference: the provided reference image is the existing Simplist lowercase wordmark; match its soft rounded geometric feel and warm color identity. Use a very small simple lowercase 'simplist' wordmark at the top of each panel, not a giant logo.
Actual app palette: pale blush #FAF2F0, terracotta #CF8169, deep clay #935C4B, warm ink #302A27, white #FEFDFD, subtle divider #F0EBE8. Typography: Poppins-like clean rounded sans serif, bold concise headlines, no serif, no script. Premium, calm, warm, tasteful.
All five panels must share a coordinated type scale, fixed top and left margins, consistent clear hierarchy and substantial app UI visibility. Every design needs one short benefit headline above one large straight-on iPhone display. Very thin graphite device frame with Dynamic Island. Realistic screen contents based on existing app, white app surfaces, terracotta accents, quiet product photography, simple flat sections. Fictional user data only. App UI can be illustrative but do not invent features such as cash funds, universal link importing, AI recommendations, price comparisons, guaranteed duplicate prevention or group payments. No star ratings, awards, app download badges or extra slogans. No oversized floating UI cards or decorative gift illustrations.
Exact five panels in left-to-right order:
1. Headline verbatim: "Your favourite gifts.\nOne simple registry." Inside phone: filled personal registry titled "Amina & Omar", small circular avatar, actions "Guest view", "Public", "Share", "12 items", and flat product rows with small elegant photos of cream dinnerware, espresso machine, linen bedding. Subtle bottom navigation. This must instantly communicate a gift registry.
2. Headline verbatim: "Discover gifts\nworth adding." Inside phone: Shop screen, search field "Search products and stores", simple category tabs, a two-column product photo grid of desirable neutral homeware gifts, terracotta small plus action on products. A quiet selection confirmation reading "Added to registry".
3. Headline verbatim: "Share your registry\nwith your people." Inside phone: same populated "Amina & Omar" registry with native iOS sharing sheet visibly open in its lower half, showing the registry link preview, "Copy", "Messages" and "Mail", minimal generic share icons. No real email addresses or personal phone numbers. Sharing must feel easy and central.
4. Headline verbatim: "See what's\nalready purchased." Inside phone: registry guest view with "Needed" and "Purchased" sections, a dinnerware row marked "Purchased 1 of 1" and a neutral terracotta checkmark, remaining products still available. This is purchase visibility, no invented delivery tracker.
5. Headline verbatim: "Find a little\ngift inspiration." Inside phone: Guides screen with beautiful editorial gift guide photos, flat guide rows titled "Wedding gifts", "Birthday favourites", "Graduation ideas", quiet dividers. Product and life-milestone photos are tasteful and realistic.
Render the headlines large and impeccably legible; reproduce wording exactly; limit small UI text so it is crisp. The result must look like an intentional professional App Store screenshot campaign.
ART DIRECTION A — SOFT EDITORIAL: warm pale blush #FAF2F0 canvas throughout all five panels; warm ink headlines left-aligned with generous breathing room; tiny terracotta brand details; phones occupy roughly lower 68 percent of each panel. Clean flat backgrounds. Small soft device shadows. Keep everything restrained, human and premium. The phone is the main evidence. No labels outside the five panels.
